source.title: nodeNameToToolName returns an empty tool name after truncation

labels.name: status:in-linear
labels.description: Issue or PR is now in Linear

source.body:
## Summary

`nodeNameToToolName` (`packages/workflow/src/tool-helpers.ts`) converts a node name into a model tool name: it replaces invalid characters, truncates to 64 characters, then strips trailing `_` / `-` left by truncation. When the first 64 characters after truncation are all `_` or `-`, the trailing cleanup wipes the entire name and returns an empty string.

## Minimal reproduction

```ts
nodeNameToToolName('-'.repeat(64) + 'Suffix'); // returns ''
nodeNameToToolName('_'.repeat(64) + 'Suffix'); // returns ''
```

For comparison, `nodeNameToToolName('a'.repeat(100))` returns `'a'.repeat(64)` and `nodeNameToToolName('a'.repeat(63) + ' more text')` returns `'a'.repeat(63)`.

## Expected behavior

Trailing cleanup after truncation may only remove trailing separators, never the whole name. The inputs above should return a non-empty, valid tool name containing only `[a-zA-Z0-9_-]` and no longer than 64 characters. Ordinary long names should still have their trailing underscore/hyphen removed (existing behavior unchanged).

## Impact

This helper is shared by ToolWorkflow, ToolCalculator, ToolCode, ToolHttpRequest, ToolVectorStore, ToolWikipedia, McpTrigger and other AI tool nodes to generate the tool name / server name sent to the model API. A node name starting with a long run of hyphens or underscores (users can name nodes freely) produces an empty tool name, which the model API rejects; the workflow then fails with an error that does not point back to the node name. The fix only affects the truncation branch.
